messages:
Sam B: FYI noticing a p95 spike after the 09:05 deploy. looks correlated with mixed prefill+decode batches hitting the same GPU.
Maya T: saw it too. tail goes from ~220ms -> ~520ms for some requests. repro on canary with pipeline: small prompt + long gen.
Ryan C: quick hypothesis: kernel selection + KV thrash when prefill jobs leave lots of KV holes and decode tries to reuse. combined batches change memory access patterns.
Anita K: agree. also saw more kernel fallbacks in logs (looped into slow fallback kernels) when batch shapes mix long prefill + short decode.
Sam B: perf-bot can you dump the kernel-selection trace for a mixed batch vs separated? include kv hit/miss counts.
perf-bot: mixed-batch trace @4100001200
perf-bot: kernel_trace: [fast_kernel x2, fallback_kernel x4] | kv_hits: 38 | kv_misses: 62 | batch_shapes: [prefill:3x256, decode:7x16]
perf-bot: separated-batch trace @4100001300
perf-bot: kernel_trace: [fast_kernel x6] | kv_hits: 88 | kv_misses: 12 | batch_shapes: [prefill-only:5x256, decode-only:5x16]
Maya T: those kv numbers are telling. mixed batches increase misses a lot — likely because prefill primes different KV offsets.
Ryan C: operational tweak: split the batcher into two admission queues at the scheduler level: prefill-queue and decode-queue. keep token_budget targets separate. ensure decode queue prefers small sequence-length kernels.
Sam B: proposed config snippet for batcher gating:
Sam B: ```yaml
batcher:
  queues:
    - name: prefill
      max_items: 64
      token_budget: 15000
      allow_mixed: false
    - name: decode
      max_items: 128
      token_budget: 8000
      prefer_kernel: small_seq_fast
  handshake_window_ms: 6
  kv_warmup_ms: 12
``` 
Anita K: handshake_window_ms increase + kv_warmup helps reduce coldspots — prefill gets a short kv-warm period before decode from same GPU joins.
Ryan C: kernel hinting: when admitting decode items, set kernel_hint=small_seq_fast; runtime then picks the fast path, avoid fallback. also prefer quantized kernel only for decode flows.
Maya T: curious about cost tradeoff. splitting queues might reduce batching efficiency for some mix workloads. can we do a dynamic admission that allows mixing only when shapes align?
Sam B: yes — implement a quick check: allow_mixed only if avg_seq_len_ratio < 1.2 AND kv_hit_rate_pred > 0.8. otherwise force separation.
Maya T: can we add a light-weight predictor? use last-1s running stats per shard to estimate kv_hit_rate_pred.
Ryan C: I'll prototype the admission rule + kernel_hint on canary. plan: A/B with 5% traffic, measure p50/p95, KV hit rate, kernel fallback counts.
perf-bot: baseline (mixed) canary: p50=48ms p95=520ms kernel_fallbacks=120/min kv_hit=0.38
perf-bot: experiment (separated + hint) canary: p50=45ms p95=185ms kernel_fallbacks=12/min kv_hit=0.86
Sam B: nice. those deltas look promising. small p50 improvement + huge p95 reduction. next: add conservative token_budget targets to avoid decode starvation.
Anita K: token_budget suggestion: prefill_target_tokens=12k, decode_target_tokens=6k for our 80% short-gen workload. adjust per-customer.
Maya T: will run a quick stress with adversarial mix (random long prefill + long decode) to ensure no regressions.
Ryan C: also logging change: add batch_shape_summary to traces and kv_warmup_flag to rows for easier postmortems.
Sam B: action items: Ryan implement admission rule + kernel_hint (ETA 1 day). Maya run stress test + canary (ETA 1 day). Anita codify token_budget defaults in policy docs (ETA 2 days). I'll monitor canary and do rollback plan.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started: 5% -> 4100001400
Maya T: noted, watching metrics :eyes:
Sam B: thanks team :thumbsup:
